extra.message: Remote Code Execution via eval — Remote code execution on the server, full system compromise. [verified: The eval() call in patient_formula_cast_251 uses a restricted globals dict, but Python's object model allows access to dangerous classes (e.g., via ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()) enabling arbitrary code execution. No input validation or sanitization is applied before eval, and the view is reachable via a GET request after passing the _wrk_gate check, which does not neutralize the inje]

Missing patient-level access control for front desk document listing — An attacker with front desk role can enumerate and view all non-internal-clinical documents across all patients, exposing sensitive medical records and PII/PHI. [verified: In document_list (line 67), front desk users (is_front_desk) are only filtered to exclude internal clinical documents, with no patient-level restriction. Unlike clinicians who use visible_patient_queryset (line 64), front desk users can enumerate all non-internal-clinical documents across all patients, violating patient-level access control and exposing PHI metadata.]

User Enumeration via Login Response Differentiation — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames/emails, aiding targeted attacks. [verified: Login returns distinct status codes for locked (429) and disabled (403) accounts vs. invalid credentials (400), letting an attacker detect valid usernames with those statuses. No rate limiting or generic error message neutralizes this.]
